"MAX-A-MILLION" offers a top prize of $1 million and thirteen prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The numbers for "MAX-A-MILLION" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
985.headline: The prize mix in this game

988.body:
The top prize count on "Emerald 10's" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If you play "Emerald 10's" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
988.headline: Top prizes are still left

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "LADY LUCK" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.

992.headline: How this game pays out

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The table below shows the full count for "$5,000 Triple Play", with every prize level included.
993.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has 111,686 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $3,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything here about "$25,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 14.
994.headline: What the prize table shows

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has two of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

If "$200,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
